title: From cold exposure to carbon uptake: individual plant responses in R’s CO₂ dataset
summary: Follow each plant’s carbon uptake across seven measured CO₂ concentrations, then compare plant-level averages descriptively. Three plants represent each population–treatment combination, so repeated measurements are not independent replicates. The source describes 14 hours of daytime chilling at 7°C, 10 hours of recovery at 20°C, and measurement at 26°C; R’s documentation instead describes overnight chilling. Concentration units remain unresolved, and measurement order may influence curve shape. No new findings are asserted.

# Cold Treatment and Carbon Uptake in R’s CO2 Dataset: Experimental Design, Measurement Provenance, and Physiological Limits

## At a glance

### What changed

- Chilled plants received 14 hours of daytime chilling at 7°C. [^S0aadb060bb3b] <!-- tempest-briefing-item: -->
- R's documentation describes the chilling treatment as occurring overnight. [^S7528fd2c1ece] <!-- tempest-briefing-item: -->
- Plants underwent 10 hours of nighttime recovery at 20°C before carbon-uptake response curves were generated. [^S0aadb060bb3b] <!-- tempest-briefing-item: -->
### Why it matters

- **Assessment:** Assess the decision implications of: Chilling had a larger observed effect on the photosynthetic CO₂ response curves of Mississippi plants than Québec plants. _(Evidence: `C_4aedd41cc0ecc97d`; confidence: medium.)_ <!-- tempest-briefing-item: -->
### Review today

- **Review:** Review before deciding: Each plant received the seven CO₂ levels in increasing, consecutive order. | Each control plant was randomly paired with a plant designated for chilling. | Three plants were measured for each population-by-chilling-treatment combination. _(Evidence: `C_2277c94eefb5869a`, `C_8b1a60b66d8f6f27`, `C_da954114dc68107b`.)_ <!-- tempest-briefing-item: -->

analyses.title: Trace individual plant responses and compare plant-level averages
analyses.question: How do individual uptake profiles and plant-level mean uptake vary across population and treatment, without assuming an undocumented matched-pair crosswalk or conducting small-sample inference?
analyses.code:
# Base R only: uses datasets::CO2, with no downloads or package installation.
x <- datasets::CO2
cat('R version:', R.version.string, '\n')
cat('datasets version:', as.character(utils::packageVersion('datasets')), '\n')
# Inspect metadata before any data.frame conversion.
cat('\nObserved units attribute of datasets::CO2, printed without reinterpretation:\n')
print(attr(datasets::CO2, 'units'))
cat('This attribute is observed dataset metadata, not independent confirmation of physical units.\n')
cat('Concentrations remain unchanged; their physical units are unresolved here.\n')
cat('Uptake units below follow the inspected R help page, not an inferred conversion.\n')

d <- data.frame(Plant = as.character(x$Plant),
                Type = as.character(x$Type),
                Treatment = as.character(x$Treatment),
                conc = x$conc, uptake = x$uptake,
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
cat('\nMissing values by column:\n')
print(colSums(is.na(d)))
stopifnot(!anyNA(d), all(is.finite(d$conc)), all(is.finite(d$uptake)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(d[c('Plant', 'conc')]))
by_plant <- split(d, d$Plant)
stopifnot(all(vapply(by_plant, function(z) length(unique(z$Type)) == 1L &&
  length(unique(z$Treatment)) == 1L, logical(1))))
grid <- sort(unique(d$conc))
stopifnot(length(grid) == 7L)
stopifnot(all(vapply(by_plant, function(z) identical(sort(z$conc), grid), logical(1))))
plants <- unique(d[c('Plant', 'Type', 'Treatment')])
plant_counts <- with(plants, table(Type, Treatment))
stopifnot(nrow(plants) == 12L, all(dim(plant_counts) == c(2L, 2L)),
          all(plant_counts == 3L))
cat('\nDataset dimensions and concentration values as stored:\n')
print(dim(d)); print(grid)
cat('\nRows per plant: repeated measurements, not independent replicates:\n')
print(table(d$Plant))
cat('\nPlant counts by population and treatment:\n')
print(plant_counts)

# Export the actual installed dataset, not reconstructed or simulated values.
utils::write.csv(x, 'co2_raw.csv', row.names = FALSE)

# Flatten aggregate output so each exported statistic has its own CSV column.
pw <- aggregate(uptake ~ Type + Treatment + conc, d,
  function(v) c(n_plants = length(v), mean_uptake = mean(v), sd_uptake = sd(v),
                minimum_uptake = min(v), maximum_uptake = max(v)))
pointwise <- data.frame(pw[c('Type', 'Treatment', 'conc')],
                        as.data.frame(pw$uptake), check.names = FALSE)
pointwise <- pointwise[order(pointwise$Type, pointwise$Treatment, pointwise$conc), ]
cat('\nPointwise descriptive summaries across plants:\n')
print(pointwise, row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(pointwise, 'co2_pointwise_summaries.csv', row.names = FALSE)

# Each plant contributes one equally weighted mean across measured levels.
pm <- aggregate(uptake ~ Plant + Type + Treatment, d, mean)
names(pm)[names(pm) == 'uptake'] <- 'mean_uptake'
pm <- pm[order(pm$Type, pm$Treatment, pm$Plant), ]
cat('\nPlant-level means across measured concentration levels:\n')
print(pm, row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(pm, 'co2_plant_means.csv', row.names = FALSE)
ps <- aggregate(mean_uptake ~ Type + Treatment, pm,
  function(v) c(n_plants = length(v), mean = mean(v), sd = sd(v),
                minimum = min(v), maximum = max(v)))
plant_summary <- data.frame(ps[c('Type', 'Treatment')],
                            as.data.frame(ps$mean_uptake), check.names = FALSE)
cat('\nDescriptive summaries of plant-level means:\n')
print(plant_summary, row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(plant_summary, 'co2_plant_mean_summaries.csv', row.names = FALSE)

contrast <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sort(unique(pm$Type)), function(tp) {
  z <- pm[pm$Type == tp, ]
  stopifnot(all(c('chilled', 'nonchilled') %in% z$Treatment))
  chilled <- mean(z$mean_uptake[z$Treatment == 'chilled'])
  nonchilled <- mean(z$mean_uptake[z$Treatment == 'nonchilled'])
  data.frame(Type = tp, chilled_mean = chilled, nonchilled_mean = nonchilled,
             chilled_minus_nonchilled = chilled - nonchilled)
}))
cat('\nDescriptive group-mean differences only; not paired differences:\n')
print(contrast, row.names = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(contrast, 'co2_descriptive_contrasts.csv', row.names = FALSE)
cat('\nNo hypothesis tests, confidence intervals, fitted asymptotes, or paired calculations are produced.\n')
cat('Concentration and increasing measurement order cannot be separated by these profiles.\n')
cat('Treatment timing: source describes 14 h daytime chilling at 7 C, then 10 h recovery at 20 C, then measurement at 26 C; R documentation describes overnight chilling.\n')
cat('These are not direct measurements during chilling.\n')

# Figure 1: consistent axes and plant-specific trajectories in each group.
groups <- unique(d[c('Type', 'Treatment')])
groups <- groups[order(groups$Type, groups$Treatment), ]
plant_palette <- c('#376C82', '#A36545', '#647C55')
ink <- '#25313A'
grid_color <- '#E7EBED'
pretty_treatment <- function(v) ifelse(v == 'nonchilled', 'Nonchilled', 'Chilled')
y_limits <- range(d$uptake)
y_pad <- diff(y_limits) * 0.06
if (y_pad == 0) y_pad <- 1
y_limits <- y_limits + c(-y_pad, y_pad)
grDevices::png('co2_response_curves.png', width = 3000, height = 2400,
               res = 300, pointsize = 12, bg = 'white')
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(5.2, 5.0, 3.0, 1.0),
    oma = c(2.0, 0, 2.8, 0), col = ink, col.axis = ink,
    col.lab = ink, col.main = ink, family = 'sans', las = 1)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(groups))) {
  z <- d[d$Type == groups$Type[i] & d$Treatment == groups$Treatment[i], ]
  ids <- sort(unique(z$Plant))
  plot(range(d$conc), y_limits, type = 'n', axes = FALSE,
       xlab = '', ylab = '',
       main = paste(groups$Type[i], pretty_treatment(groups$Treatment[i]), sep = ' | '))
  abline(h = pretty(y_limits), col = grid_color, lwd = 0.8)
  axis(1, at = grid, labels = grid, cex.axis = 0.8)
  axis(2, cex.axis = 0.9)
  box(col = '#B8C1C6')
  mtext('CO2 concentration (stored values; units unresolved)', side = 1, line = 3.1, cex = 0.8)
  mtext('Uptake (micromol m^-2 s^-1)', side = 2, line = 3.2, las = 0, cex = 0.85)
  for (j in seq_along(ids)) {
    zz <- z[z$Plant == ids[j], ]; zz <- zz[order(zz$conc), ]
    lines(zz$conc, zz$uptake, type = 'b', pch = c(16, 17, 15)[j],
          col = plant_palette[j], lwd = 1.8, cex = 0.7)
  }
  legend('bottomright', legend = ids, col = plant_palette[seq_along(ids)],
         pch = c(16, 17, 15)[seq_along(ids)], lty = 1, lwd = 1.8,
         bty = 'n', cex = 0.85)
}
mtext('Individual plant uptake profiles', outer = TRUE, side = 3, line = 1.0,
      cex = 1.25, font = 2)
mtext('Lines connect repeated observations; concentration increased in measurement order.',
      outer = TRUE, side = 1, line = 0.6, cex = 0.85)
grDevices::dev.off()

# Figure 2: open a new device only after closing the first one.
mean_limits <- range(pm$mean_uptake)
mean_pad <- diff(mean_limits) * 0.12
if (mean_pad == 0) mean_pad <- 1
mean_limits <- mean_limits + c(-mean_pad, mean_pad)
group_colors <- ifelse(groups$Treatment == 'chilled', '#376C82', '#A36545')
grDevices::png('co2_plant_level_comparison.png', width = 3000, height = 2100,
               res = 300, pointsize = 12, bg = 'white')
par(mar = c(6.5, 5.5, 4.5, 1.5), oma = c(2.0, 0, 0, 0),
    col = ink, col.axis = ink, col.lab = ink, col.main = ink,
    family = 'sans', las = 1)
plot(c(0.5, nrow(groups) + 0.5), mean_limits, type = 'n', axes = FALSE,
     xlab = '', ylab = '', main = 'Plant-level uptake: individuals and group means')
abline(h = pretty(mean_limits), col = grid_color, lwd = 0.8)
axis(2)
axis(1, at = seq_len(nrow(groups)),
     labels = paste(groups$Type, pretty_treatment(groups$Treatment), sep = '\n'),
     tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.95)
box(col = '#B8C1C6')
mtext('Plant mean uptake (micromol m^-2 s^-1)', side = 2, line = 3.6, las = 0)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(groups))) {
  z <- pm[pm$Type == groups$Type[i] & pm$Treatment == groups$Treatment[i], ]
  z <- z[order(z$Plant), ]
  offsets <- seq(-0.13, 0.13, length.out = nrow(z))
  points(i + offsets, z$mean_uptake, pch = 21, bg = group_colors[i],
         col = 'white', lwd = 0.8, cex = 1.6)
  text(i + offsets, z$mean_uptake, labels = z$Plant, pos = 3,
       offset = 0.7, cex = 0.8, col = ink)
  segments(i - 0.23, mean(z$mean_uptake), i + 0.23, mean(z$mean_uptake),
           col = ink, lwd = 2.5)
}
mtext('Dots: individual plants   |   Short horizontal lines: group means',
      side = 3, line = 0.7, cex = 0.9)
mtext('Each plant mean weights the seven measured concentration levels equally; no inferential intervals.',
      outer = TRUE, side = 1, line = 0.5, cex = 0.85)
grDevices::dev.off()

cat('\nExported files:\n')
print(c('co2_raw.csv', 'co2_plant_means.csv', 'co2_pointwise_summaries.csv',
        'co2_plant_mean_summaries.csv', 'co2_descriptive_contrasts.csv',
        'co2_response_curves.png', 'co2_plant_level_comparison.png'))
print(utils::sessionInfo())
assumptions: The installed datasets::CO2 object is the accessible quantitative input. Its software version, units attribute, and structure are printed; it is not claimed to be a verified transcription of every value in the paper’s OCR table.
Each plant was measured at seven CO₂ concentrations. Three plants were measured for each population-by-chilling-treatment combination. The code validates these features.

Repeated observations are summarized within plants before describing between-group differences. Pointwise standard deviations describe dispersion across plants at a concentration, not independent replication across concentration levels.

The source describes random pairing of control plants with plants designated for chilling, but no explicit crosswalk from the paper’s numbered plants to R’s Plant identifiers is supplied. Similar suffixes are not evidence of pairing; paired calculations are omitted.
Group-mean contrasts are descriptive only. No hypothesis tests, confidence intervals, or small-sample inferential claims are produced.
Each plant received the seven CO₂ levels in increasing, consecutive order. Curve shape cannot separate concentration effects from possible sequence effects.

The inspected R help page defines uptake as carbon dioxide uptake rate in micromoles per square metre per second. This documentation-based interpretation is distinct from the units attribute printed directly from the installed object.
Concentration values are preserved exactly as stored. Observed metadata are not treated as external confirmation of concentration units; conflicting labels or units are not silently reconciled.
The plant mean equally weights the measured concentration levels. It is not an integral over concentration, time-integrated carbon gain, or fitted physiological capacity.

The source-supported sequence is 14 hours of daytime chilling at 7°C, then 10 hours of recovery at 20°C, then measurement at 26°C. R’s documentation instead describes overnight chilling. This conflict is retained; profiles are not described as direct measurements during chilling.

All generated files use accepted CSV or PNG formats. The two graphics devices are closed separately, with no graphics-parameter restoration after device closure. Only base R and bundled packages are used, without installation, network, environment-variable, or credential access.

illustrations.title: From cold exposure to leaf measurement
illustrations.prompt: Create a beautiful, highly legible editorial scientific schematic as a high-resolution landscape PNG, not a photograph. Use a warm off-white background, generous whitespace, fine charcoal typography, restrained blue-green foliage, cool blue for cold exposure, and muted amber for recovery. Show three clearly separated stages connected left to right by simple arrows. Stage 1: a stylized generic plant in a cool chamber, labeled 'Cold exposure' and '14 hours at 7°C'. Stage 2: the same generic plant motif in a neutral recovery chamber, labeled 'Recovery' and '10 hours at 20°C'. Stage 3: a close-up leaf enclosed in a simplified gas-exchange chamber connected by tubing to an abstract instrument, labeled 'Leaf gas-exchange measurement' and '26°C'. The repeated plant motif indicates stages, not sample counts. Add the clear heading 'From cold exposure to measurement' and a small but readable footer: 'Conceptual schematic — not experimental evidence'. Include a readable note: 'Source describes daytime chilling; R documentation describes overnight chilling.' Do not imply that uptake was measured during cold exposure. Do not depict treatment effects, numerical results, data plots, bar charts, sample counts, geography maps, species-specific identifying features, or undocumented apparatus details. Keep apparatus deliberately schematic and all text crisp and readable at report-embedding size.
illustrations.alt: Conceptual three-stage schematic: cold exposure for 14 hours at 7°C, recovery for 10 hours at 20°C, and leaf gas-exchange measurement at 26°C. A note preserves the disagreement between daytime chilling in the source and overnight chilling in R’s documentation. No results or sample counts are depicted.
illustrations.caption: Conceptual schematic, not a photograph or experimental evidence. The source describes 14 hours of daytime chilling at 7°C followed by 10 hours of recovery at 20°C and measurement at 26°C; R’s documentation instead describes overnight chilling. The schematic shows the reported sequence for chilled plants, not measurements during chilling or a complete comparison of treatment protocols.
